title: The length of the quotient by powers of an element avoiding the minimal primes is at most n times the length modulo the element itself

standard_prerequisites.name: Finite length of a module supported at the closed point, and additivity of length in a short exact sequence
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes P well defined and gives the inequality in the induction step.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness on the left of the sequence R/x^{n-1}R -> R/x^nR -> R/xR -> 0 when x is a nonzerodivisor
standard_prerequisites.use: Upgrades the inequality to the exact recursion and hence to equality.

core_obligations: Note that since dim(R) = 1 each quotient R/x^nR has dimension zero, so length_R(R/x^nR) is finite for every n (proof lines 37990-37993).
Record the base cases: P(0) = length_R(R/x^0R) = length_R(0) = 0, and the statement holds for n = 1 (proof lines 37994-37996).
For n >= 2, use the exact sequence R/x^{n-1}R -> R/x^nR -> R/xR -> 0 with the first map multiplication by x (proof lines 37997-38002).
Apply additivity of length to get P(n) <= P(n-1) + P(1), and use the induction hypothesis P(n-1) <= (n-1)P(1) to conclude P(n) <= n P(1) (proof lines 38003-38007).

For the equality statement, note that when x is a nonzerodivisor the displayed sequence is also exact on the left, so that P(n) = P(n-1) + P(1) for all n >= 1, hence P(n) = n P(1) (proof lines 38009-38012).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring (R, m) and an element x in m contained in no minimal prime of R, and asserts that the function P(n) = length_R(R/x^n R) satisfies P(n) <= n P(1) for all n >= 0, with equality for all n when x is a nonzerodivisor (source lines 37978-37988). The proof first notes that since the dimension is one, each R/x^nR has dimension zero and hence finite length, so P is defined (proof lines 37990-37993). It then argues by induction on n: P(0) = length_R(0) = 0 and the case n = 1 is immediate, and for n >= 2 the proof uses the exact sequence R/x^{n-1}R -> R/x^nR -> R/xR -> 0, where the first map is multiplication by x (proof lines 37994-38002). Additivity of length in this sequence gives P(n) <= P(n-1) + P(1), and the induction hypothesis P(n-1) <= (n-1)P(1) then yields P(n) <= n P(1), completing the induction step (proof lines 38003-38007). The equality statement is the substantive sharpening: when x is a nonzerodivisor the displayed sequence is also exact on the left, so one gets the exact recursion P(n) = P(n-1) + P(1) for all n >= 1, hence P(n) = n P(1) (proof lines 38009-38012). The non-routine content is the exactness of the short sequence and the resulting two-sided length computation.
